newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse sees trade in new equity issues.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse sees trade in new equity issues.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) saw trade last week in newly issued shares of three Yugoslav banks, the bourse said on Tuesday.
Union banka, AIK banka and Srpska Komercijalna banka together listed a total of 18 million dinars ($3.16 million) worth of shares and sold 14.9 million dinars worth, BSE said.
"All those shares listed on the bourse were sold as part of pre-arranged deals," a broker told Reuters.

To meet rules set by the Yugoslav Securities Commission (YSC) last November and aimed at speeding up development of the local financial market, banks and companies are obliged to sell part of their issued shares on the bourse if the issue is to qualify as successful.
The issuing bank or company has 90 days to complete the sale. If not, the issue is annulled.
In practice, banks and companies issue new stock to increase their capital and sell it to known buyers.
But those shares do not trade on the secondary market, mainly due to fears that the market price would be much below the face value, analysts said.

The BSE, which also makes markets in financial instruments and commodities, did not trade equities in 1996. The only two shares listed and traded in 1995 were those of Investbanka and Sintelon. Both were delisted late in 1996 after months of non-trading.

Since the beginning of 1997, shares have sporadically reappered on the BSE. Beside Union banka, AIK banka and Srpska Komercijalna, two other banks -- Prva Preduzetnicka and Jugobanka Krusevac -- have also listed their stock. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
